claims.text: CI: QT-prolonging drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, such as erythromycin, pimozide and quinidine.
claims.quote: Coadministration of other drugs known to prolong the QT interval and which are metabolized via the enzyme CYP3A4 such as erythromycin, pimozide, and quinidine are contraindicated in patients receiving fluconazole.

claims.text: Moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor and strong CYP2C19 inhibitor: monitor narrow-therapeutic-window drugs metabolized this way;
claims.quote: Fluconazole is a moderate CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor. Fluconazole is also a strong inhibitor of CYP2C19. Patients treated with DIFLUCAN, who are also concomitantly treated with drugs with a narrow therapeutic window metabolized through CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, should be monitored for adverse reactions associated with the concomitantly administered drugs.

claims.text: the effect persists 4 to 5 days after stopping.
claims.quote: The enzyme inhibiting effect of fluconazole persists 4 to 5 days after discontinuation of fluconazole treatment due to the long half-life of fluconazole.

claims.text: Rare serious hepatotoxicity, usually but not always reversible on stopping:
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN hepatotoxicity has usually, but not always, been reversible on discontinuation of therapy.

claims.text: use with caution in liver dysfunction;
claims.quote: (1) Hepatic injury: DIFLUCAN should be administered with caution to patients with liver dysfunction. DIFLUCAN has been associated with rare cases of serious hepatic toxicity

claims.text: stop if signs of liver disease develop.
claims.quote: DIFLUCAN should be discontinued if clinical signs and symptoms consistent with liver disease develop that may be attributable to DIFLUCAN.
